Here is some overview information about this project which you may find useful.

# Overview

This is a Web Application framework inspired by <https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/apps/aspnet>
but built for <https://www.typescriptlang.org/> & <https://deno.com/>.

## Deno

This project targets <https://deno.com/>, **NOT** <https://nodejs.org/>,
<https://bun.com/> or any other JavaScript runtime.

_It is a non goal to support these other runtimes._

### Runtime Permissions

When you need to run deno, always use `-A`.

That is to say, to make things easier just assume that all runtime permissions
are needed for any of our scripts.

_read more: <https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/security/#permissions>_

### JSR

All TypeScript dependencies should be installed from <https://jsr.io/> where available.
If a suitable package can not be found on JSR, you may use <https://www.npmjs.com/> as a last resort.

#### Standard Library

Furthermore we should prefer to use dependencies from the Standard Library. eg: `@std/{package}`.

Deno provides a standard library written in TypeScript. It is a set of standard
modules that can be reused by programs, allowing you to focus on your application
logic rather than "reinventing the wheel" for common tasks. All of the modules in
the Deno Standard Library are audited by the core team and are guaranteed to work
with Deno, ensuring consistency and reliability.

read more: <https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/std/>

#### Notable Exceptions

- <https://zod.dev/>: We use the NPM version (<https://www.npmjs.com/package/zod>)
  to provide greater compatibility with existing Zod tooling.

## Tests

All tests should use the standard Deno.test APIs. **DO NOT** use the `@std/testing/bdd` API.

When writing new tests use the `@std/expect` library as opposed to `@std/assert` or any other framework.

Unit tests should be added to files alongside the modules they are testing
with-in the `src/` folder, with the `.test.ts` suffix. That is to say, if we
wanted to writes tests for items exported from `src/foo.ts` we would create the
file `src/foo.test.ts` and add tests cases there.

Integration or end to end tests should be added to `.test.ts` files under the
`tests/` folder, separate from our Unit Tests.

_read more: <https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/testing/>_

### Running Tests

- To run all tests, execute: `deno test -A --coverage ./packages/{package_name}/**/*.test.ts`

- To run all Unit tests, execute: `deno test -A ./packages/{package_name}/src/**/*.test.ts`

- To run all Integration & E2E tests, execute: `deno test -A ./packages/{package_name}/tests/**/*.test.ts`

- To run all tests in a given file, execute: `deno test -A ./path/to/file.test.ts`

- To run a single test, update the test case definition to use `Deno.test.only`
  & then execute the test file. eg: `deno test -A ./src/foo.test.ts`. Once you are
  finished debugging that test case reset the test case definition back to `Deno.test`.

### Test Coverage

80% test coverage is acceptable but we should strive for 90% or greater test coverage.

## MonoRepo

This is a monorepo, where all Deno packages reside in `packages/`.
This is configured in the root `deno.json` workspace file.

Each package is structured as:

- `src/`: Folder for source code

- `tests/`: Folder for integration & end to end tests

- `CHANGELOG.md`: This file will exist if the package has been released at least once.
  It is generated by <https://github.com/cocogitto/cocogitto>.

- `README.md`: The packages main reference documentation.

- `deno.json`: The packages deno config file.

- `Taskfile.yaml`: Automation tasks for the package.

### Tooling Management

All developer tooling is managed & installed with [Pixi](https://pixi.sh/).
Also see <https://prefix.dev/>, the organization behind Pixi.

You can find our pixi config at the root of the repository in the `pixi.toml` file.

### Task Runner of Choice

While pixi does come with a built-in Task Runner, we prefer to use <https://taskfile.dev/>.

- There is a root `Taskfile.yaml` for tasks that operate across the entire repo.
- Each package has `./packages/*/Taskfile.yaml` for tasks that operate specifically against that package.

**DO NOT** use the built in Taskfile includes functionality (<https://taskfile.dev/docs/guide#including-other-taskfiles>),
it does not scale very well & can introduce unexpected bugs, specifically related to variable scope.

Instead prefer to just call task child processes. eg: `task -t ./packages/foo/Taskfile.yaml bar`

### Conventional Commits

This project adheres to the <https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/> standard.

And uses <https://github.com/cocogitto/cocogitto> to enforce the standard as
well as help orchestrate our release process.
